subject: Novacare pricing corridor & procurement lanes — follow-up
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Fiona Chen <fiona.chen@novacare.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T09:07:00Z
Subject: Novacare pricing corridor & procurement lanes — follow-up

Fiona — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we can align procurement and finance on the next steps.

Key items we discussed:
- Monthly consumption profile: teams expect variable usage but planning for a recurring range rather than fixed commit. You mentioned a likely operating corridor rather than a hard commit.
- Procurement thresholds: small purchases (cc) vs standard PO vs formal contract/MAA. You said PO > $25k typically needs procurement review; > $75k goes to legal and vendor underwriting.
- Unit economics target: you asked for a ballpark $/1M tokens so you can map to internal engineering budgets.

Proposed framing from Redwood to make procurement decisions simple:
1) Self-serve/CC lane: up to $5k/month (quick onboarding, no PO)
2) Standard PO lane: $5k–$25k/month (standard terms, 30–45 day PO)
3) Contracted lane: > $25k/month (SLA, MAA, legal review; typical lead time 3–4 weeks)

Unit economics (initial guidance): for the Novacare workload profile you shared (median prompt length ~1.5k tokens, interactive inference mix) we estimate an effective price band of $380–$520 per 1M tokens for the models we demoed. Committed volume discounts apply above 10M tokens/month.

Next steps I propose:
- Can you confirm the procurement gate numbers (PO thresholds) you referenced?
- If PO threshold is accurate, would the Novacare procurement team prefer a formal quote that lists the three lanes above?
- I’ve attached a one-page MAP and a sample pricing spreadsheet for your internal finance model.

If that looks right I’ll loop in our procurement lead (Rishi) to start a short PO-ready quote and the legal checklist for the contracted lane.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Novacare_MVP_pricing.xlsx (xlsx), Novacare_MAP_v1.pdf (pdf)

From: Fiona Chen <fiona.chen@novacare.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Novacare Procurement <procurement@novacare.ai>
Date: 2026-08-30T10:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Novacare pricing corridor & procurement lanes — follow-up

Thanks Vanessa — quick confirmations below.

- Procurement thresholds: accurate high level. Our internal rules are: card up to $3k; PO for $3k–$30k (procurement review, single approver); legal review kicks in for recurring spend > $50k/month or new vendor > $50k ARR.
- We’re not ready to commit > $50k/month yet; realistic short term corridor is $8k–$30k/month depending on pilot traction.
- For unit economics, finance wants a baseline $/1M tokens figure that maps to a typical month at 15–20M tokens.

Please send a PO-ready quote for the $8k–$30k lane and the standard MSA highlights for > $30k. Procurement@novacare.ai is the right inbox for the official PO routing.

—Fiona
Fiona Chen
Head of Product | Novacare Health
fiona.chen@novacare.ai | +1 415-222-3344

Subject: Re: Novacare pricing corridor & procurement lanes — follow-up

Adding pricing detail per Vanessa’s ask so Fiona and procurement have a clean PO-ready starting point. I’ll keep options conservative so finance can stress-test.

Suggested commercial options (draft figures — final numbers will go on formal quote):
A) Flex (no commit) — retail usage pricing
   - $/1M tokens: $520
   - Monthly effective: variable; good for proof-of-concept, higher per-unit cost

B) Commit (12-mo, tiered) — moderate discount for predictable usage
   - 5–10M tokens/month: $420 per 1M tokens
   - 10–20M tokens/month: $360 per 1M tokens
   - 20M+ tokens/month: $300 per 1M tokens

C) Pilot retainer (one-off blended) — for an initial pilot with a small committed bucket
   - Example: $20k/month retainer = ~45–50M token-equivalent at blended pricing for pilot burst (price and exact token mapping noted in quote)

Procurement lane mapping (to align with Fiona’s thresholds):
- Card: up to $3k — retail flex pricing (Option A)
- PO: $3k–$30k — either Option A or B depending on commitment level; we can prepare a PO-ready line item for Option B at the $8k–$30k corridor Fiona mentioned
- Contract/MAA: > $30k — full SLA, legal addenda, and tiered commit pricing (Option B/C)

Vanessa — I’ll draft a one-page quote that lists the PO line item (Option B, sample tiers) and a separate MSA summary for > $30k. Rishi and I can join the procurement call if Novacare wants to run through legal/finance questions.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Solutions | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

Appreciate the clarity — this is helpful. We’d like the PO-ready quote as discussed for the $8k–$30k corridor. Specific asks from procurement/finance:

1) One-line PO item that maps to "Redwood inference usage (flexible corridor)" with a not-to-exceed monthly cap.
2) Baseline $/1M tokens to use for internal burn modeling (Karthik’s Option B tiers are good — please label them clearly).
3) Expected lead time for contract/MAA if we move to > $30k/month (we typically see 3–4 weeks as you noted; confirm whether Redwood has a standard SOW or MAA template).

If you can send the PO-ready line item and a one-page MSA summary by end of day Monday our procurement team will slot a short review on Tuesday.

Fiona
